audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for idol-food, knowledge puffing up, love building, one Divine/one Lord, conscience, liberty wounding weak sibling.

verses.restored: Now concerning things offered to idols: we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds.

familiar.text: Now as touching things offered unto idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

modern.text: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

original.text: Περὶ δὲ τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων, οἴδαμεν ὅτι πάντες γνῶσιν ἔχομεν. ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ.

verses.restored: If anyone thinks to have known anything, one has not yet known as it is necessary to know.

familiar.text: And if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know.

modern.text: The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.

original.text: ⸀εἴ τις δοκεῖ ⸀ἐγνωκέναι τι, ⸀οὔπω ⸀ἔγνω καθὼς δεῖ γνῶναι·

verses.restored: But if anyone loves the Divine, this one has been known by him.

familiar.text: But if any man love God, the same is known of him.

modern.text: But the one who loves God is known by God.

original.text: εἰ δέ τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν θεόν, οὗτος ἔγνωσται ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore concerning eating things offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no Divine except one.

familiar.text: As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one.

modern.text: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.

original.text: Περὶ τῆς βρώσεως οὖν τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ ὅτι οὐδεὶς ⸀θεὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς.

verses.restored: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, just as there are many gods and many lords,

familiar.text: For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,)

modern.text: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),

original.text: καὶ γὰρ εἴπερ εἰσὶν λεγόμενοι θεοὶ εἴτε ἐν οὐρανῷ εἴτε ἐπὶ γῆς, ὥσπερ εἰσὶν θεοὶ πολλοὶ καὶ κύριοι πολλοί,

verses.restored: yet for us there is one Divine, the Father, from whom are all things and we into him; and one Lord, Jesus Messiah, through whom are all things and we through him.

familiar.text: But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.

modern.text: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ἡμῖν εἷς θεὸς ὁ πατήρ, ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ εἷς κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, διʼ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς διʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: But not in all is this knowledge. Some, by habit until now toward the idol, eat as idol-offered, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

familiar.text: Howbeit there is not in every man that knowledge: for some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat it as a thing offered unto an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled.

modern.text: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

original.text: Ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν πᾶσιν ἡ γνῶσις· τινὲς δὲ τῇ ⸀συνηθείᾳ ⸂ἕως ἄρτι τοῦ εἰδώλου⸃ ὡς εἰδωλόθυτον ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτῶν ἀσθενὴς οὖσα μολύνεται.

verses.restored: Food will not present us to the Divine; neither if we do not eat do we lack, nor if we eat do we abound.

familiar.text: But meat commendeth us not to God: for neither, if we eat, are we the better; neither, if we eat not, are we the worse.

modern.text: But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.

original.text: βρῶμα δὲ ἡμᾶς οὐ ⸀παραστήσει τῷ θεῷ· οὔτε ⸂γὰρ ἐὰν φάγωμεν, περισσεύομεν, οὔτε ἐὰν μὴ φάγωμεν, ὑστερούμεθα⸃.

verses.restored: But watch lest somehow this authority/liberty of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.

familiar.text: But take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to them that are weak.

modern.text: Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.

original.text: βλέπετε δὲ μή πως ἡ ἐξουσία ὑμῶν αὕτη πρόσκομμα γένηται τοῖς ⸀ἀσθενέσιν.

verses.restored: For if anyone sees you, the one having knowledge, reclining in an idol temple, will not the conscience of the one being weak be built up into eating idol-offerings?

familiar.text: For if any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idol’s temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;

modern.text: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?

original.text: ἐὰν γάρ τις ἴδῃ σὲ τὸν ἔχοντα γνῶσιν ἐν εἰδωλείῳ κατακείμενον, οὐχὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτοῦ ἀσθενοῦς ὄντος οἰκοδομηθήσεται εἰς τὸ τὰ εἰδωλόθυτα ἐσθίειν;

verses.restored: For the weak one is destroyed by your knowledge, the sibling because of whom Messiah died.

familiar.text: And through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died?

modern.text: So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.

original.text: ⸂ἀπόλλυται γὰρ⸃ ὁ ἀσθενῶν ⸀ἐν τῇ σῇ γνώσει, ⸂ὁ ἀδελφὸς⸃ διʼ ὃν Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν.

verses.restored: Thus sinning/misaligning against the siblings and striking their weak conscience, you sin/misalign against Messiah.

familiar.text: But when ye sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ.

modern.text: By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

original.text: οὕτως δὲ ἁμαρτάνοντες εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τύπτοντες αὐτῶν τὴν συνείδησιν ἀσθενοῦσαν εἰς Χριστὸν ἁμαρτάνετε.

verses.restored: Therefore if food causes my sibling to stumble, I will certainly not eat flesh into the age, so that I may not cause my sibling to stumble.

familiar.text: Wherefore, if meat make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth, lest I make my brother to offend.

modern.text: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.

original.text: διόπερ εἰ βρῶμα σκανδαλίζει τὸν ἀδελφόν μου, οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἵνα μὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν μου σκανδαλίσω.

translation_notes: Knowledge versus love is the governing contrast: accurate theology without love can still destroy a sibling.
Conscience is treated as a tender communal reality, not as mere ignorance to be mocked.
